cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Make the Choice Rewrite the Past
cards.instruction: Make them choose between options whose consequences reinterpret an earlier promise, refusal, or agreement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Choose the overseas job or our shared shop. Then we'll know what 'we'll build something' meant. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said that before the offer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Yes. This choice gives the old sentence its ending.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're making a job sound like a goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm asking whether your promise has room for the shop without you.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 forces a career/shop choice tied to old promise, but A3 confidence and adjustment are not enacted as cooperative tactics.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 dates the promise; A3 insists on retrospective meaning; B4 calls it goodbye and A5 asks about the promise without a clear workable choice.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 resist a loaded framing rather than merely answering setup questions.

heightening.evidence: A5 raises room-for-shop-without-you but leaves whether A accepts a third arrangement obscure.

specificity.evidence: A1 overseas job and shared shop are clear; A3 sentence-ending metaphor and A5 room metaphor obscure the exact request.
